title: India Sends an IIT-Educated, Pakistan-Tested Diplomat to London at a Pivotal Moment for the Diaspora
excerpt: Periasamy Kumaran, a 1992-batch IFS officer who served in Islamabad during the Mumbai attacks era, takes charge as High Commissioner to the UK — home to 1.8 million people of Indian origin
body:
New Delhi has appointed one of its most seasoned diplomats to the most consequential diaspora posting in the world. Periasamy Kumaran, a 1992-batch Indian Foreign Service officer who was most recently Secretary (East) in the Ministry of External Affairs, has taken charge as India's High Commissioner to the United Kingdom, succeeding Vikram Doraiswami, who has moved on to become India's Ambassador to China.

The appointment, announced on 26 March 2026, places an IIT Madras-educated engineer-turned-diplomat at the helm of a mission that serves the largest Indian diaspora in Europe — approximately 1.8 million people of Indian origin who live, work and study across Britain.

## A Career Shaped by Crisis Postings

Kumaran's career reads like a map of India's most sensitive diplomatic relationships. After entering the IFS in 1992, he served at the Indian Embassy in Cairo from 1994 to 1997, studying Arabic at the American University in Cairo alongside his diplomatic duties. He then moved to Tripoli, Libya, from 1997 to 2000, followed by a posting at the Indian Embassy in Brussels.

His most consequential early assignment came in 2007, when he was posted as Counsellor to the Indian High Commission in Islamabad — a role he held through the aftermath of the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks, one of the most volatile periods in India-Pakistan relations in a generation. He subsequently served at the Indian Embassy in Washington from 2009 to 2011, and as Deputy High Commissioner in Colombo, Sri Lanka, from 2011 to 2014.

Before his current appointment, Kumaran served as India's Ambassador to Qatar from 2016 to 2020, where he managed relations during a period of significant Gulf diplomatic upheaval, and as High Commissioner to Singapore from 2020 to 2023, a posting where he oversaw deepening economic ties between the two nations.

## Why This Posting Matters for NRIs

The UK is home to one of the most politically and economically influential Indian diasporas anywhere in the world. Indian-origin individuals led non-EU migration to Britain in 2025, and the community's influence extends deep into Parliament, the judiciary and the corporate world. Illinois Supreme Court Justice Sanjay T. Tailor is just one example of diaspora figures reaching the highest levels of their professions.

But the relationship is also turbulent. Indian students now make up one of the largest international student cohorts in British universities, even as visa restrictions have tightened. Net migration from India saw an 80,000 drop due to new policy changes, according to recent data. Meanwhile, the Indian High Commission in London has faced security incidents, including vandalism that prompted the MEA to summon the British diplomat responsible.

Kumaran arrives at a moment when the UK is also trying to position itself as a partner in India's technology ambitions. In January 2026, UK Deputy Prime Minister David Lammy and AI Minister Kanishka Narayan led a delegation to India's AI Impact Summit, signalling London's interest in deepening tech collaboration.

## The India-UK Free Trade Question

The elephant in the room remains the India-UK Free Trade Agreement, which has been under negotiation since 2022 and remains unfinished. The deal would directly affect Indian businesses, students and professionals in Britain — from tariffs on textiles and whisky to the mutual recognition of professional qualifications that could open doors for thousands of Indian-trained doctors, engineers and accountants.

Kumaran's trade experience from his Qatar and Singapore postings — both of which involved navigating complex economic partnerships — will be tested immediately.

## Doraiswami's Legacy

Kumaran succeeds Vikram Doraiswami, who is widely regarded as one of India's most effective public-facing diplomats. Doraiswami was vocal on social media, engaged directly with diaspora concerns and navigated the politically sensitive extradition case of Nirav Modi. He now takes on what is arguably India's most strategically important bilateral relationship as Ambassador to China.

For the 1.8 million Indians in Britain — and the tens of thousands of students, workers and families whose lives are shaped by the decisions made at India House on Aldwych — the new High Commissioner's track record suggests a diplomat who has been tested in the hardest rooms and emerged with his credibility intact.
